text: Pride, vanity, envy, ambition, and malice are the ungrateful foes that combat merit and integrity; though for a while they may triumph, to the injury of the just and good, the steady, unwearied perseverance of virtue and honor will finally prevail over them. He who can retire from a public life to a private station with a self-approving conscience, unambitious of pomp or power, has little to dread from the machinations of envy, the snares of treachery, the malice of dissimulation, or the clandestine stabs of calumny.
author: Abigail Adams
reference: Familiar Letters of John Adams and His Wife Abigail Adams
locator: Letter 263, Abigail Adams to John Adams, 26 February, 1780
